s: RFID communication primarily takes place through radio waves exchanged between:
o: A satellite and a television broadcaster only
A biometric sensor and a printer only
A battery and a display screen
A tag carrying identity data and a reader

s: Which one of the following correctly describes an active RFID tag?
o: It has its own battery and transmitter and can broadcast itself over a long range.
It stores no identity data and functions only as a visual label.
Its battery powers only the chip and it must use the reader’s field to reply.
It has no battery and only reflects the reader’s field over a short range.
x: An active RFID tag has its own battery and transmitter, broadcasts by itself and generally offers a longer range. A semi-passive tag uses its battery for the chip but relies on the reader’s field to reply.
tq: Distinguish active, passive and semi-passive tags by their power source and response method.
sec: ■ RFID and wearables - passive vs active tags, wearable functions  [APPSC]

s: A semi-passive RFID tag differs from an active RFID tag because the semi-passive tag:
o: Uses its battery to run the chip but uses the reader’s field to reply
Has no internal power and cannot contain identity data
Has an independent transmitter and broadcasts over a long range
Uses only a satellite signal for communication
x: A semi-passive tag’s battery powers its chip, but it still uses the reader’s field to send its response. An active tag has its own battery and transmitter.
tq: Focus on the exact distinction between battery use and transmission capability.
sec: ■ RFID and wearables - passive vs active tags, wearable functions  [APPSC]
